whatItIs.text: A fresh, acid-set cheese from South Asia — non-ageing and famously non-melting, which is why it grills and curries without slumping.

historyNote.text: Paneer's origin is genuinely disputed: doubtful Vedic references, a 10th-century Kannada text describing buffalo-milk cheese coagulated with plant roots, and theories of Persian or Afghan origin — India's National Dairy Research Institute credits Afghan and Iranian invaders; a Portuguese acid-setting influence in the 17th century is also argued.

howToChoose.text: Choose blocks that look moist and ivory with a clean dairy smell, not sour or slimy; firmer blocks fry better, softer ones crumble for fillings.

storage.text: Keep in the fridge, submerged in water if the pack is open — refreshed daily.

useItUp.text: Cube and fry paneer for curries and snacks, or crumble it into fillings.

substitutions.note: saltier and squeakier; rinse or soak first
the standard vegan swap; press and fry
